title: adaptive-prefetch-experiment-notes
body:
Summary:

Short notes from an ad-hoc investigation into a throughput regression on prod that looks correlated with the adaptive prefetch/prefix-caching knobs introduced in the new cbatch optimizer (nov rollout). This is a personal scratchpad — rough, chronological breadcrumbs and commands I ran.

Symptom (user-visible):
- Sudden QPS->tokens/sec drop during 2026-02-18 afternoon window; client apps reported elevated p95/p99 and occasional 503s.
- Baseline numbers (pre-regression): cluster tokens/sec ~ 18k, p95 ~ 220ms, p99 ~ 540ms. During incident: tokens/sec dipped to ~9.5k, p95 climbed to 480ms, p99 spiked >1200ms.

Initial hypothesis: mis-tuned adaptive prefetch window (prefetch_ms) + aggressive inflight_limit interaction is causing starvation and increased cold KV-cache misses which cascade into higher latency and lower throughput.

Recent changes that could be relevant:
- Nov rollout: adaptive prefetch feature enabled for redwood/7B-v2 and redwood/13B-compat by default (rbctl flag rollout).
- 2026-02-17: small config bump to default inflight_limit from 8 -> 4 to reduce memory pressure on smaller SKUs (ticket INF-2317).

Timeline & breadcrumbs (chronological):
- 2026-02-18 13:45 PST: infra alert - tokens/sec drop, spike in server-side latencies.
- 2026-02-18 13:47: started investigating with basic metrics.
- 2026-02-18 13:50: rolled emergency canary to route traffic to older config (prefetch disabled) — partial improvement.
- 2026-02-18 14:20: reproduced locally in staging with similar traffic shape.

Commands tried (copied from shell history):
- rbctl config get batching
  -> batching: {"adaptive_prefetch": true, "prefetch_ms": 200, "inflight_limit": 4, "kv_prefetch": "on"}
- kubectl -n inference logs deploy/serve-runtime -c cbatch --since=2h | grep -i prefetch | tail -n 50
  -> [2026-02-18T14:10:03Z] WARN cbatch: prefetch_window_ms=200, inflight_limit=4 -> window alignment mismatch, trimming prefetch set
  -> [2026-02-18T14:10:04Z] ERROR kvcache: missing prefix cache for model redwood/7B-v2, key=a1b2... (cold miss)
- curl -sS http://localhost:9000/metrics | grep cbatch | grep -E "prefetch|inflight|kvcache"
  -> cbatch_prefetch_attempts_total 12345
  -> cbatch_prefetch_drops_total 4321
  -> cbatch_inflight_limiter_drops_total 2793
  -> kvcache_misses_total 9921
- kubectl -n inference exec -it deploy/serve-runtime -- ps aux | grep cbatch
- rbctl rollout status --service serving-runtime --since 2026-02-17
- patched configmap to temporarily set prefetch_ms=0:
  kubectl -n inference patch configmap cbatch-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefetch_ms":"0"}}'

Observed outputs & log snips (important):
- From logs (2026-02-18T14:10):
  [2026-02-18T14:10:03Z] WARN cbatch.prefetch: alignment mismatch: window=200ms, inflight_limit=4, avg-latency=95ms -> trimming to 50ms
  [2026-02-18T14:10:04Z] ERROR cbatch.kvcache: cold miss: model=redwood/7B-v2 prefix="user-ctx-xyz" latency=320ms
  [2026-02-18T14:10:06Z] INFO cbatch.batch: batch formed size=1 -> flushed due to deadline; downstream load increased

- Metrics snapshot (15m window around incident):
  - tokens/sec: 18k -> 9.5k (drop ~47%)
  - cbatch_prefetch_attempts_total: increased 2.3x
  - cbatch_prefetch_drops_total: increased 8x (spikes aligned with drop)
  - kvcache_misses_total: increased 4x (cold miss storm)

Experiments run and results (staging + small prod canary):
1) Disable adaptive prefetch (prefetch_ms=0):
   - tokens/sec recovered to ~16.5k (not fully to pre-incident), p95 improved to ~270ms.
   - kvcache_misses returned closer to baseline.
2) Increase inflight_limit to 12 (on canary nodes):
   - tokens/sec partially recovered to ~14.5k, p95 ~320ms, but memory pressure increased on smaller nodes -> OOM risk on micro instances.
3) Set prefetch_ms=50 and inflight_limit=8:
   - best compromise in staging: tokens/sec ~17.8k, p95 ~240ms, kvcache_miss rate lower than default.

Interpretation / refined hypotheses:
- The adaptive prefetch logic assumes a moderate inflight_limit to amortize the cost of prefetching KV prefixes. When inflight_limit was reduced to 4, the prefetch window of 200ms caused the system to overcommit speculative prefetches relative to actual active requests, which increased contention on the KV cache and produced many cold misses. Those misses are expensive (disk/remote calls) and caused the batching engine to flush small batches (size=1) more often which reduces throughput and increases p95/p99.
- Secondary factor: model-specific prefix keys for redwood/7B-v2 have higher fanout, so cold miss penalty larger than for other models; this amplified impact.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- 14:30: set prefetch_ms=0 via configmap patch for all prod nodes (temporary emergency). This recovered most throughput.
- 14:45: rolled partial config with prefetch_ms=50, inflight_limit=8 to canary subset. Monitored for 45min; metrics stable.

Proposed longer-term fixes (roadmap items):
- Tweak adaptive prefetch heuristics to account for current inflight_limit and recent kvcache_miss rate (avoid blind prefetch when inflight is low).
- Add circuit-breaker to throttle prefetch when kvcache_miss_rate > threshold for a sliding window.
- Improve prefix key locality by hashing hot prefixes to a local fast cache (short-term: increase in-RAM kvcache size for hot prefixes).
- Add a telemetry gauge that correlates prefetch_attempts vs inflight_limit and exposes a signal used by autoscaler to avoid pathological combos.

Small experiments to run (next week):
- A/B with prefetch_ms=0 / 50 / 100 across similar traffic slices and measure kvcache_miss rate and batch sizes.
- Synthetic microburst test: replay production traces with reduced inflight_limit values (1..16) and capture batch formation histograms.

Next steps / TODO (my personal checklist):
- [ ] Write up short postmortem draft for INF-2317 (include timeline and config diffs).
- [ ] Open a PR to modify adaptive prefetch logic to read inflight_limit at runtime and scale back prefetch aggressiveness when inflight_limit < 6. (assign to Evan)
- [ ] Add metric: cbatch_prefetch_backpressure_ratio (ask SRE for 30d retention).
- [ ] Schedule follow-up with product to decide default for new clusters (prefetch enabled vs disabled).
- [ ] Document emergency rollback steps in runbook (where to patch configmap, rbctl commands).

Notes & oddities to investigate later:
- Why did prefetch_drops_total increase faster than prefetch_attempts? (looks like a logic path that 'drops' queued prefetch requests on alignment mismatch — find code path in optimizer).
- The cold misses show a repeated pattern of the same prefix keys being missed across different nodes; check whether prefix hashing is consistent across instances (possible bug in prefix key sharding).
- Check if tokenizer changes altered average seq-length distribution earlier in Feb (fewer tokens per request => different batching dynamics).

Quick emergency commands to remember (handy for runbook):
- Disable prefetch globally: kubectl -n inference patch configmap cbatch-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"prefetch_ms":"0"}}'
- Re-enable safe defaults: rbctl config set batching.prefetch_ms=50 batching.inflight_limit=8
- Watch metrics: curl -sS http://metrics.internal:9000/metrics | grep -E 'cbatch|kvcache'

End of scratchpad.

-- Maya

(Will convert into a short postmortem and runbook once we validate fixes and run the A/B experiments.)
